_note: The school model (GDD 4.9.3, session S1; scripts/core/school_system.gd). The calendar itself (real 2026-27 dates and the rules for later years) is data/school.json; this file holds the model: the stages, the subjects, the starting grades by the creation answer, the two weekly life settings, how grades drift, the tests, the report cards and the life load. NEUTRAL = IDENTICAL: a normal school day at Normal / Normal has a life load of exactly 0, and at 0 the game is today's game to the last digit (the code does not even run). Life load is a number per day in 'points': positive = a heavier day (fatigue recovers slower, colds a little more likely, injuries a little more likely), negative = a lighter one (holidays). All numbers here are Claude's first guesses (estimated), to be tuned in B1; the user's decisions of 2026-10-17 are in GDD 4.9.3 'Built (step S1)'.

stages._note: The school year that starts in the autumn of year Y is grade Y - birth year - grade_offset (born 2012: grade 8 in 2026-27). Grades 8 and 9 are yläkoulu; after grade 9 the placeholder 'secondary' runs (the calendar and the life load go on, the grades are frozen) until S3 builds lukio / urheilulukio / vocational school. `scale` multiplies every positive part of the life load (grade 9 has more homework); `exam_weeks` = the stage's big exam weeks (user 2026-10-17: none in yläkoulu, only single tests; the rule format is ready for S3: each item {before: christmas | winter | end, weeks: n} = the Mon-Fri school week n weeks before that break's first free day).

subjects._note: The yläkoulu subjects of the report card (GDD 4.9.3). academic = the subjects of the application average (lukuaineet, S3); practical subjects are graded from the term's work without tests. In real schools music, art, crafts and home economics are partly electives in grades 8-9; S1 keeps them all on the card as the GDD lists them.

answers._note: The creation answer 'How do you do at school?' (background_questions.json school_answer): `start` = the starting grade average (GDD 4.9.3: ~9.0 / 8.5 / 7.5 / 6.8 / 6.3), `natural` = the average the grades drift to at Normal effort. 'Good grades through hard work' starts above its natural level (keeping it costs more effort); 'Couldn't care less' a little below (unused talent). Older saves have only school_level: `from_level` maps it.

aptitude._note: Each subject has a hidden aptitude: the subject's natural level = the answer's natural average + a roll (normal, sd, at most max away), re-centred so the academic subjects (and the practical ones) average the answer's level exactly. PE: + pe_bonus (an athlete), + sports_class with the 'A sports class at school' answer. Rolled once from the career's own dice (name + birth date; the global dice untouched).

grades._note: Every school day each subject's level drifts towards its target: level += (target - level) x (1 - 0.5^(1 / half_life_days)), so half the way in half_life_days school days (~a school year). target = natural + effort shift + focus shift, kept inside min..max. GDD 4.9.7 targets: Normal holds the average +-0.3 a year, Heavy +0.5, Light -0.5 (= half of the shift in a year). Focus subjects (at most focus_max): + focus_shift each; every other academic subject - focus_others per focus subject (the study time moves).

tests._note: Single tests (kokeet): each academic subject has per_term tests a term (autumn: the start to the Christmas break; spring: after Christmas to the end), placed at even points of the term's school days plus a roll (jitter_sd school days), never in the first skip_days school days. Tests cluster naturally around the same points (like period ends). With an exam week in the term (S3), each subject's last test moves into it. A test's score = level + a roll (noise_sd) - stress (from stress_from: up to stress_penalty at 100), kept inside 4..10, rounded to round_to (8+ = 8.25, 8½, 9- = 8.75). The week's tests: more than normal_per_week tests in a Mon-Sun week make it a busy test week (life load on its test days, stress).

report_cards._note: A report card on the last school day before the Christmas break (`christmas`) and on the last day of the school year (`spring`; in grade 9 the final certificate, `final`). Academic subjects: round(tests_weight x the term's test average + (1 - tests_weight) x the level), practical subjects: round(level); whole grades 4-10. The card keeps `average` (every subject) and `academic_average` (the application average of S3).

settings._note: The two weekly life settings (GDD 4.9.3; the player sets them in S2's School page). Study effort = the grades (grades.effort_shift) and the life load of school days; free time (user 2026-10-17: motivation vs rest) = Lots: time with friends, motivation pulls up but later nights add life load; Little: more rest, motivation pulls down. Neither changes what is trained.

effort.name: Light
effort.text: The minimum: grades slide, school takes less out of you.

effort.name: Heavy
effort.text: Extra study every evening: grades rise, but school days get heavier.

free_time.name: Little
free_time.text: Home early, to bed early: more rest, but it gets dull.

free_time.name: Normal
free_time.text: Some time with friends, some rest.

free_time.name: Lots
free_time.text: Out with friends a lot: good for motivation, but late nights on school days.

life_load._note: The day's life load, in points (0 = a normal school day at Normal / Normal = today's game). Parts: a weekday off school in a break or the summer (holiday_weekday; user 2026-10-17: holidays = relief), and on SCHOOL days only: study effort, free time, a double day = two separate practices (two sessions that are not add-ons; drills, strides and the like ride along in the same practice, so the coach's Monday 'easy run + drills' is no double day), each test on a day of a busy test week, a day of an exam week (S3). Weekends are 0. Positive parts x the stage's scale. Double days are free on holidays and weekends (and in S3 in the urheilulukio's morning-practice slots).

effects._note: What the life load does (user 2026-10-17: mild). Fatigue: the day's keep (the share of fatigue carried to tomorrow, Training.daily_keep) + keep_per_point x load (an exam day of 2 points: ~4 % more fatigue built up over a week). Colds: the day's chance x (1 + illness_per_point x load), never below illness_min. Injuries (overuse and bad-luck): x (1 + injury_per_point x load) for a positive load only (Mann 2016, Hamlin 2019: more injuries in academic-stress weeks; older athletes than ours, so mild). Stress: the Sunday drift's pull = the coming week's life load summed over its days / 7 x stress_per_point; holidays pull it down. Busy test week ahead: stress news busy_week_news on the Sunday before (exam week ahead: exam_week_news). Motivation: free time Lots pulls + motivation_lots, Little - motivation_little.

texts._note: Lines of the stress / motivation rows (MindSystem.pulls, the MIND panel) and of the news. {n} = a count.

pulls.free_lots: Lots of free time: late nights
pulls.motivation_lots: Lots of free time with friends
